label: D2 after a rewarded repeat of a2, early/mid episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2), and only when this trial chose a2. It also needs the previous trial to have been a2 too (a stay; it never fires after a1, prev_action == 1) and rewarded (prev_reward == 1 holds 95% of the mass). It is also strongly gated by episode time: rate is about 10% in trials 3-49, falls off by 50-59, and is zero after trial ~65. The agent gets no clock input, so this must reflect slow drift in its hidden state (or a dependence on how confident it is in a2), not an observed variable. All variables are observed at D2. Magnitude: the largest activations (~1.0) come on rare transitions to S1 after a rewarded a2 trial; common S2 steps sit around 0.2-0.5. It never fires at D1 or GO, after an a1 choice, or late in the episode. Dev F1 0.80 (P 0.75, R 0.86, mass recall 0.94). Dropping the episode-time condition cuts F1 to 0.54. The misses are mostly low-amplitude D2 steps where the previous trial was unrewarded.

issues: The explanation leaves out a large systematic class of false positives. When the previous a2 trial was rewarded after a RARE transition (prev_common == 0, so it reached S1 and was paid), the unit is silent. Adding prev_common==0 to the original predicate gives dev precision 0.0017 over 6052 predicted steps (test precision 0.003 over 6749 steps), about a third of all its false positives. The unit needs the previous a2 trial to have been COMMON and rewarded (prev_common==1 subset: precision 0.84). The label 'after a rewarded repeat of a2' therefore overclaims.

The predicate's main time condition checks out. The unit fires only at D2 and only on a2 trials, and is essentially never active after prev_action==a1 (17 of 58k active steps). It is zero after trial 70, about 0.002 at trials 60-69 and 0.022 at 50-59, with prev_reward==1 carrying 95% of the activation mass. Dropping the time condition is clearly worse (prev_reward==1 at ep_trial>=55 has precision 0.02).

Smaller systematic false positives: when the hidden good state is S1 (the agent keeps choosing a2 after a reversal), precision is 0.36 (5482 predicted). The unit is also silent at maximal a2 confidence: no activity at all for choice < -8.91. This probably also explains why long runs of rewarded a2 trials stay inactive in the false-positive windows.
The cutoff ep_trial < 55 is a little loose. With the prev_common fix, < 50 gives a higher test F1 (0.858 vs 0.842).

No future variables are used, which is correct. The magnitude claim (the largest activations are rare S1 arrivals after a rewarded a2 trial, and common S2 arrivals sit around 0.2-0.5) matches the top windows.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 of an a2 trial after a common-rewarded a2 trial (an outcome that confirms a2), early or mid episode only (trials < ~50); silent after rare-rewarded a2 trials
